title: If you bought Micron every day when the market closed and sold it the next morning when it opened, since 1990, you'd be up over 138 million percent.

recreating.summary: @joe.investss · "The stock market is broken" (overnight returns) · https://www.instagram.com/p/Ddo1OMSIZeo/ · 1,673 likes and 344 comments on a 137K-follower account

lines.text: If you bought Micron every day when the market closed and sold it the next morning when it opened, since 1990, you'd be up over 138 million percent.
Now, imagine you did the exact opposite.
You bought when the market opened and you sold when the market closed.
That same exact trade would be down over 99 percent.
And apparently, Micron isn't the only stock that does this.
A research paper found the same phenomenon across hundreds of stocks.
So what's actually going on?
There's two different crowds trading at two different times.
Regular people tend to trade around market open, reacting to whatever news came out overnight.
Big institutions trade during the day and into close because that's where liquidity is.
And the research says that the biggest portions of stock returns actually happen while the market is closed.
So if you're only trading between open and close, you might be missing the entire point.
And if you want to see my entire portfolio for completely free common stocks, then I'll send it over to you.

notes: **Recreating:** @joe.investss · https://www.instagram.com/p/Ddo1OMSIZeo/ · copy its rhythm: the number said and shown in the first 3 seconds (title typed on letter by letter, chart already on screen), a hard cut on "Now, imagine you did the exact opposite", another on "isn't the only one", the open loop "So what's actually going on?" said straight to camera, and a new graphic or number every 2 to 4 seconds even between cuts.

**Layout:** Qube screen pinned in the top third (1080×640) the whole way through, Joshua below. Full screen only for the paper title card and the end screen. Captions 1–3 words, centred at chest height, key numbers in gold. Captions already show every spoken word, so the on-screen text below only adds what isn't said: exact numbers, dates, the rule, the source.
**Times** are estimates at Joshua's pace (3.2 words a second). Re-time to the real take. Cut every pause in the edit.

**Before recording anything:** Joshua needs a Qube login. Every Qube run below is typed in plain English into Qube's Build step. Don't show any emails, API keys or account details on screen.

rows.what: Micron, buy at the close, sell at the open
rows.how: 1. Chrome, full screen, zoom 125%, no tabs or bookmarks. Open Qube and start a new strategy. 2. Type exactly, don't paste: `Buy Micron (MU) at the close every trading day and sell it at the next day's open. Start with $1. Test it on all daily prices from January 2, 1990 to October 22, 2026. No trading fees.` 3. Run the backtest. 4. Hold 3s on the result with the chart showing. **CHECK: the total return must read about +145,000,000% (over 300 million percent), and $1 must end at about $1.45 million. If Qube won't start at $1, use $10,000 and check the percent only. If the percent is different, stop and send Mark a screenshot.** **Backup if Qube's Micron prices start later than January 2, 1990:** don't change the dates to make it fit. Write down Qube's earliest Micron date exactly as Qube shows it, run the same sentence from that date, hold 3s on the result, and send Mark the screenshot and the date. The hook number and line 4 then get rewritten from that run before the edit.
